one_month_reasoning: Two scheduled events fall in the window. (1) Micron reports fiscal Q4 2026 after the close on 2026-09-30 (guide ~$50B revenue, capex guide for FY27 above mid-$40B); its FY27 capex number moves memory-equipment names on Oct 1. The capex bar is already high, so I treat it as symmetric. (2) Lam's own Sept-quarter report, expected around Oct 21-22 (estimated date), against a guide of $8.1B / $2.15 EPS that was set above consensus. Peers (AMAT's Q4 guide of $10.25B, ASML's capacity adds for 2027) point to a beat and a solid December guide. But in September the stock fell from ~$438 to ~$324 on worries about how long AI capex lasts and on higher yields, not on company news. That macro and sentiment driver can extend either way. I center the distribution at ~$326, slightly above spot for a modest expected beat, with monthly sigma ~17%. That is a bit under the 65%/3.5 rule because the realized-vol figure is inflated by a 150% rally. I add fat tails and no strong directional call.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (NTM EPS at Sept 2027 of ~$11.5 x 27x = $311, weight 0.6) and FCF yield (CY2027 FCF/share ~$7.9 at a 2.5% yield = $316, weight 0.4), plus a small premium for the 2028 visibility that peers describe. The multiple steps down from today's ~35x FY27 consensus because by Sept 2027 the market will be pricing a peak-cycle year.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS as of Sept 2027 ~$11.5 x 27x

inputs_detail.derivation: Lam sees CY26 WFE in the low $150Bs. Sell-side CY27 estimates run $180-205B (Wells ~$190B, JPM $205B, Citi $200B bull). SEMI's older $135B is stale. I take ~$190B, supported by customer capex: TSMC 2027 capex est. $75-85B, memory big-3 capex $146B in 2027, Micron FY27 capex above mid-$40Bs, SK hynix $38B plan.

Annualizing the Q1 FY27 guide gives $8.6. Consensus FY27 is $9.32. A ~25% WFE step-up in CY27, SAM share rising toward the high-30s% and gross margin moving from 52% toward mid-50s lift EPS ~25% into the Oct-27 to Sep-28 NTM, giving ~$11.5. I haircut this for a possible 2028 digestion and China curbs (sources 13, 14).

Today the stock trades at ~35x FY27 consensus ($324/$9.32). The September sector selloff shows how sensitive that multiple is to AI-capex durability doubts. For late-cycle NTM earnings I compress to 27x, still above the historical high-teens to low-20s range because customers (sources 8, 10) describe visibility into 2028.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: CY2027 revenue ~$35B x 28% FCF margin / 1.25B shares = ~$7.9 FCF/share at a 2.5% yield

inputs_detail.derivation: FY26 revenue of $23.2B came to ~18% of the average WFE in that period (~$130-150B). At an 18.5% ratio (small share gain per management) on ~$190B CY27 WFE, revenue is ~$35B.
Operating margin guide is 39.5%. After ~15% tax, capex and working-capital build during a ramp (headcount up 1,800 in a quarter), FCF runs around 28% of revenue.
Peers AMAT and ASML trade on similar AI-driven peak-growth expectations. A 2.5% yield on peak-cycle FCF matches the ~27x earnings multiple used above.

bear.story: Worries that AI capex is peaking become a reality. Hyperscaler spending pauses, and memory prices roll over in H1 2027 as record capex ($146B for the memory big-3) adds supply. Customers push out tools, China curbs widen under the June-2026 FDPR rule, and the market prices a 2028 WFE decline. That means ~$9 trough-ish EPS at 20-21x.

base.story: CY27 WFE grows ~20-25% to ~$185-195B, led by TSMC N2/A16, DRAM/HBM and NAND conversions, where Lam's etch/dep share is highest. Lam earns ~$11-12 on NTM, but the multiple compresses toward 28-29x as the cycle matures.

bull.story: Supply-constrained memory (SK hynix calls 2027 the tightest year ever) and TSMC capex of $85B+ push CY27 WFE past $200B with visibility into 2028. Lam reaches high-30s SAM share, and NAND upgrades plus new greenfield NAND fabs accelerate. EPS runs ~$14 and the stock re-rates to its prior $438 high and beyond at ~35x.

thesis_break_reason: About $215 is ~-34%, below the pre-August-earnings breakout zone and ~23x current-year consensus EPS. At that price the market would be pricing an outright WFE decline in 2027: a memory-capex cut or a TSMC capex reset, or a major new China restriction. That would be more than the sentiment and yield-driven multiple swings seen in September.

reasoning: Industry-lane read: every link in the chain is signalling a stronger 2027. Customers: TSMC's equipment needs are up ~1.9x in six months, and sell-side puts 2027 capex at $75-85B. Micron guides FY27 capex above the mid-$40Bs, SK hynix has a $38B fab plan, and the memory big-3 are expected to spend ~$146B in 2027. Peers: AMAT's Q4 guide is $10.25B with semis systems up >30% in CY26. Suppliers: ASML is adding 30% EUV/DUV capacity for 2027 and expects memory sales up >75%. Lam itself raised CY26 WFE to the low $150Bs and is guiding $8.1B next quarter (+20% q/q). Sell-side CY27 WFE sits at $180-205B. Against this, the stock already prices much of it at ~35x FY27 consensus of $9.32. The September drawdown ($438 to $324) was sector-wide and tied to AI-capex durability and rates, not Lam news. Memory-cycle history shows equipment stocks peak before the WFE peak. China curbs are tightening (Hua Hong halt, June FDPR rule). Fair value ~$318 blends forward P/E ($11.5 x 27x) and FCF yield. Distribution: median ~$335, slightly above spot, as strong fundamentals are offset by expected multiple compression. The spread is a lognormal mixture (80% sigma 0.45, 20% sigma 0.68), giving an effective ~50% vol. That is below the 65% trailing realized figure, which was inflated by the 150% rally, but well above a typical large-cap's 25-35%, because this is a high-beta cyclical near a potential peak. Scenarios are bear $190 (25%), base $335 (50%) and bull $520 (25%). Research was limited to ~12 web queries/fetches. The SEMI press release returned 403, so SEMI figures come from secondary reports.
